title: Momentum
overview: Apply conservation of momentum and impulse to collisions between particles. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Use linear momentum p=mv as a vector in one dimension.
Apply conservation of momentum to direct impacts.
Handle particles that coalesce after collision.
Interpret signs and check whether the proposed post-collision motion is possible.

definitions.definition: Mass multiplied by velocity; its direction follows the velocity.
A collision in which motion is along one straight line.
Total momentum is unchanged when external impulse during the interaction is negligible.
Bodies join and move with a common velocity after impact.
The collection of bodies chosen for a conservation equation.

sections.title: Momentum as a vector
content: Choose a positive direction and write each momentum as mv with a signed velocity. Momentum has units kg m s⁻¹. A negative result means motion opposite to the chosen direction, not negative speed.
bullets: Use velocities immediately before and immediately after impact.

sections.title: Conservation equation
content: For an isolated impact, total momentum before equals total momentum after. Include every body in the chosen system and keep the same positive direction on both sides.
bullets: Internal impact forces cancel in the system total.
External forces are neglected only over the short collision time.

sections.title: Coalescing particles
content: If masses m₁ and m₂ stick together, their final mass is m₁+m₂ and they share velocity v: m₁u₁+m₂u₂=(m₁+m₂)v. The kinetic energy usually decreases, even though momentum is conserved.
bullets: Do not conserve kinetic energy unless justified.
Check whether v lies between the incoming signed velocities when appropriate.

sections.title: Scope and interpretation
content: This component examines one-dimensional direct impact and conservation. Impulse and coefficient of restitution are not required by the 2026–2027 Paper 4 syllabus. Focus on a clean before/after diagram and a signed momentum equation.
bullets: Report direction with the final velocity.
A body may reverse direction after impact.

examTips: Draw a before/after line diagram with arrows before writing momentum equations.
State the final direction when a calculated velocity is negative.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to combine masses when particles stick.
Assuming momentum conservation means kinetic-energy conservation.

quickRecall.question: Why are velocities signed in momentum work?
quickRecall.answer: Momentum is a vector, so direction must be represented.

quickRecall.question: What common velocity applies after coalescence?
quickRecall.answer: Both bodies move with one velocity v and combined mass m₁+m₂.

quickRecall.question: Is kinetic energy always conserved in Paper 4 impacts?
quickRecall.answer: No. Momentum is conserved for the isolated system; kinetic energy may be lost.

quickRecall.question: Are impulse and restitution required here?
quickRecall.answer: No; they are outside the stated 2026–2027 Mechanics content.
